title: Rest-Day Workshop Credits — Set 1401
statement: A community studio offers one workshop per day with the listed credits. Attending a workshop requires resting the following day, so no two selected day indices may be adjacent. Return the largest total credits you can earn. You may skip every workshop; an empty schedule earns zero. The input is one object { credits }.
constraints: Each credit value is an integer from 0 through 40.

examples.explanation: For {"credits":[5,9,5]}, the result is 10. For each day compare skipping it with adding its credits to the optimum from two days back. Keep only the two previous optima.
For {"credits":[0,0]}, the result is 0. For each day compare skipping it with adding its credits to the optimum from two days back. Keep only the two previous optima.

hints.content: Taking the largest single workshop first may block a better pair.
At each day, compare attending with skipping.
Attending uses the best total ending before the preceding day.
Skipping retains the best total for all previous days.
Use current = max(oneBack, twoBack + credit), then shift the two stored totals.

solutions.title: Enumerate the candidates
solutions.intuition: Enumerating all allowed choices gives a small-input correctness oracle.
solutions.approach: Enumerate every subset with a bit mask, reject adjacent selected bits, and maximize the selected credit sum. The fourteen-day bound keeps exhaustive validation small.
solutions.pseudocode: Enumerate every subset with a bit mask, reject adjacent selected bits, and maximize the selected credit sum. The fourteen-day bound keeps exhaustive validation small.
commonMistakes: Greedily choosing the largest credit value.
Updating twoBack before computing the current value.
Forcing a workshop on an empty schedule.
